response.sql: SELECT AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(CAST(replacement_cost AS DOUBLE) / rental_rate) AS avg_cost_to_rate_ratio FROM film WHERE length > 112;

assumptions.assumption: "More than 112 minutes" is a strict inequality (length > 112), and the filter excludes films with NULL length, so NULL lengths never enter either average.
The group is all qualifying films taken together, so avg_length is the plain mean of their lengths and no grouping column is used.

The ratio is computed per film as replacement_cost / rental_rate and then averaged. The division is cast to DOUBLE so MySQL's DECIMAL division does not truncate the result to its default extra precision. rental_rate is never zero in the data (minimum 0.99), so no division by zero occurs, and AVG skips any NULL ratios.
